title: Full SSRF with user role on endpoint /api/v1/retrieval/process/web via location redirect
summary: > [!IMPORTANT] > Note: This advisory describes the same SSRF vulnerability as GHSA-c6xv-rcvw-v685 (CVE-2025-65958), which was published Dec 4, 2025. Both reports identify the SSRF in /api/v1/retrieval/process/web, and the same fix (commit 02238d3113e966c353fce18f1b65117380896774, released in v0.6.37) addresses both. @Mosstrow's report (filed Sept 9, 2025) chronologically predates the canonical advisory's publication; the duplicate disposition reflects publication order rather than filing order, and is a consequence of triage queue depth rather than a judgment on the reports. Affected versions on the canonical advisory (<=0.6.36) supersede the range here (<=0.6.26). ### Summary Open WebUI is vulnerable to Server-side Request Forgery (SSRF) via the /api/v1/retrieval/process/web endpoint. An attacker with user privilege can manipulate the URL to any external destination without validation, enabling the endpoint to initiate requests to the specified URL and relay the response. Direct internal fetch is blocked via "ENABLE_LOCAL_WEB_FETCH to protect against SSRF attacks" https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/1862/files But it's possible to use a location php script to redirect the flow internally bypassing this security. This vulnerability permits unauthorized access to internal services and could potentially allow command execution by accessing instance secrets. ### Details Direct internal fetch is blocked via "ENABLE_LOCAL_WEB_FETCH to protect against SSRF attacks" https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/1862/files This could be bypassed by redirect location header. ### PoC `` Internal call success: Location redirect: ### Impact This vulnerability permits unauthorized access to internal services and could potentially allow command execution by accessing instance secrets. ### Recommendation Implement additional security measures to prevent redirects
